text.p: Venezuelan cement company Vencemos, a unit of Mexico's Cemex, will raise the value of its exports by nearly 10 percent to $100 million in 1997, Vencemos President Victor Romo told Reuters Tuesday.
Exports in 1996 totaled $91.5 million, up from $76.1 million in 1995.
"Exports in 1997 will be slightly above those in 1996. We expect an increase of two percent in volume, which means they will be about $100 million," Romo said after an annual shareholders meeting.
A tough economic adjustment program at home hit domestic demand for Vencemos' products last year, forcing it to look abroad to expand sales, he said.
"The volume of exports (in 1996) was a record for Vencemos," Romo said.
The company expected to make "similar" net profits in 1997 to the 47.451 billion bolivars ($99 million) reported from 1996.
